# paper-finder-student-mcp

> Academic paper search MCP server through OpenAlex. No key needed. Free and open source MCP server for AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Copilot and others).

## Setup
- Run with npx -y paper-finder-student-mcp
- Add it to your MCP config. Claude Desktop reads claude_desktop_config.json, Cursor reads ~/.cursor/mcp.json, VS Code reads .vscode/mcp.json and calls the key servers. All three start the server with command npx and args ["-y", "paper-finder-student-mcp"].
- No key or account. Optional OPENALEX_EMAIL for OpenAlex's polite pool.
- Papers are identified by DOI (10.xxxx/yyy) or OpenAlex id (W followed by digits).

## Data
- All results come from OpenAlex (https://openalex.org), a free open catalog of scholarly works, so the papers are real, not invented.
- Every tool reads OpenAlex directly, so there is no key needed and no account.
- Author names are looked up in the OpenAlex author records, so the papers come back even when the name on the paper is written in another form.
- A search can be ordered by citation count or by date, limited to journal articles, preprints or book chapters, and every result carries a one line abstract.
- The citing, the related and the reference lists carry a one line abstract as well, so a paper can be judged from the list before it is opened.
- The citation graph runs both ways: `find_citing_papers` gives the papers that cite a paper and `paper_references` gives the papers a paper cites.

## Tools
- search_papers: Search scholarly papers by keywords. Returns title, authors, year, venue, citation count, DOI, a one line abstract and a free to read link when one exists. The results can be ordered, so you can get the most cited papers on a topic or the newest ones, and they can be limited to one kind of paper. Inputs: query (required keywords), from_year (optional earliest publication year), open_access_only (optional, false by default), type (optional, journal_article, preprint or book_chapter), sort (optional, relevance for the OpenAlex order, cited_by_count:desc for the most cited papers first, or publication_date:desc for the newest papers first), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'find the most cited papers on spaced repetition since 2020.'
- get_paper: Details for one paper, including the abstract and a free to read link when one exists. A wrong or unknown reference returns a not found error that suggests searching by title or checking the DOI format. Inputs: paper (optional, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), doi (optional, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539 or a doi.org link, no OpenAlex ids). Give paper or doi, and paper wins if you give both. Example prompt: 'show me the abstract of DOI 10.1038/nature14539.'
- find_open_access_pdf: Finds a free to read copy of one paper and returns the link, preferring a PDF over a landing page. When OpenAlex has no free copy it says so in plain words instead of failing. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807). Example prompt: 'find a free PDF of this paper, DOI 10.1038/nature14539.'
- find_related_papers: Lists the papers that OpenAlex lists as related to a given paper, so you can find more work on the same topic. Every result carries a one line abstract, so you can judge a paper before you open it. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'what papers are related to DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762?'
- find_citing_papers: Lists the papers that cite a given paper, newest first. Every result carries a one line abstract, so you can judge a paper before you open it. This is the other half of the citation graph that paper_references covers, so a literature review can walk the graph in both directions. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'who cited DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1706.03762?'
- paper_references: The papers that one paper cites, which is the other half of the citation graph that find_citing_papers covers. Every result carries a one line abstract, so you can judge a paper before you open it. Use it to read the bibliography of a paper, to find the source a result came from, or to work backwards from a paper to the earlier work it builds on. Inputs: paper (required, a DOI like 10.1038/nature14539, a doi.org link, or an OpenAlex id like W2741809807), sort (optional, cited_by_count:desc for the most cited references first, or publication_year:asc for the oldest references first), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'what papers does DOI 10.1038/nature14539 cite?'
- list_author_papers: Papers by one author, most cited first. The name is looked up in the OpenAlex author records first, so initials, a different order of the name parts and other spellings of the same person still find the papers, and the papers are then taken from that author id. When OpenAlex has no record for the name, the papers are matched by the name as it is written on them. Inputs: author (required, the author name, for example Jane Doe, or an OpenAlex author id like A5108843829), from_year (optional earliest publication year), open_access_only (optional, false by default), limit (optional, 1 to 25, default 8). Example prompt: 'list papers by John Dewey on education since 1950.'

The deprecated tools cited_by, related_papers, get_paper_by_doi and get_related_work still work as aliases for find_citing_papers, find_related_papers and get_paper with doi, so saved prompts keep working. New prompts should use the tools listed above.

Each tool description states its inputs and one example prompt.
